hero.title: The Learning Goal
hero.description: I wanted to understand what happens 'under the hood' of search engines. Instead of reaching for a library, I built this experiment to explore Data Structures, Big O notation, and the trade-offs between RAM and Disk.

cards.title: The Question
cards.text: Why do standard database queries get slow as data grows? I wanted to see the impact of O(n) linear scans firsthand.

cards.title: The Experiment
cards.text: I implemented a manual Inverted Index (HashMap) in Node.js to see if I could achieve O(1) lookup times without external tools.

cards.title: The Lesson
cards.text: I learned that while RAM is fast, it's scarce. I had to strictly type my data models to keep memory usage efficient.

steps.desc: Server boots & loads the dataset into memory (simulating a hot cache).
Tokenizer breaks titles into keywords & maps them to internal IDs.
Search queries intersect these ID sets to find matches instantly.
Final results are retrieved directly from the in-memory store.
